Grammar extra
More on verb +direct object + prepositional phrase
With these verbs,use forin the prepositional
Will you bake a cake for me?
phrase: bake, buy,cook, draw, find, make,
I'm painting a picture for my father.
and paint.
Withmost other verbs,useto:give,hand,
I didn't send a gift to him this year.
lend,offer,owe,pay,read, send, show, and
We handed all our money to the clerk.
write.
Withbringand take,you can use foror to,
I've brought some flowers for you. (=They're a gift.)
but the meaning is different.
Can I borrow your laptop? I'll bring it back to you later.
About
Rewrite the sentences using a direct object + prepositional phrase.Then use the ideas to
you
write true sentences of your own.
1. I always bake my sister a cake on her birthday.
2. I never give my friends money. I prefer to hand them a nicely wrapped gift.
3. When friends invite you for dinner, it's nice to offer your host a small gift.
4. On special occasions, I'll often cook my family a nice meal.
5. If you want to give a friend who has everything a gift, a magazine subscription is a good idea.
6. When I get greeting cards, I always show my family the messages.
7. When I have to send someone a gift in the mail, I always choose something small.
8. I once made a friend an unusual gift. I drew him a picture of his cat.
9. My parents once bought me an underwater camera for my birthday.
Passive sentences
In the passive, either the indirect object or the direct object can become the subject of the sentence
